citation: An ecological perspective on children's play with digital technologies in South Africa and the United Kingdom (Journal of Psychology in Africa)
mechanisms: Digital engagement is validated by educational utility because technology is valued primarily as a route out of poverty rather than for entertainment

Shared device scarcity creates parent-child congruence because limited hardware creates overlapping digital practices that put parents in a stronger position to support their child's use, though this does not guarantee active co-play
Inconsistent connectivity mandates offline functionality because intermittent access renders always-online products impractical despite perceived need
Home-school projects bridge resource gaps because classroom device scarcity necessitates extending digital ecologies into domestic spaces
Intergenerational mediation enables adoption because skilled elders provide the family-supported knowledge transfer necessary to navigate technology
objection_patterns: Does this help with education or is it just for entertainment?
Can we use this together on our shared device?
Will it work when the internet is not consistent?
Can my grandmother help me understand how to use this?
confidence: Qualitative survey and case study data from South Africa and UK; mechanisms derived from author interpretation of parental and teacher perspectives, magnitudes unknown
